newsitem.title: EGYPT: Housing, banking sectors boost Egypt shares.
newsitem.headline: Housing, banking sectors boost Egypt shares.

text.p: Healthy gains in the housing and banking sectors boosted Egyptian share prices on Thursday by 4.15 percent, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority overall index rose 12.42 points to 314.2 on average volume of 48.35 million pounds ($14.22 million).

"The market is moving up as we expected in the first week of the year," said Neveen el-Tahry of Delta EABbrokerage. "This is the end of the week so I would have thought that heavy trading would have started on January 8. But it started earlier than we expected.
"Also, the bourse removed price caps from two housing stocks which allowed the shares to move up to the levels they should be at. This made a difference," she added.

Tahry was referring to price ceilings that the stock market board imposed last week on Medinet Nasr Housing and Development and Heliopolis Housing and Development because it believed the two stocks were overpriced.
Medinet Nasr was the most active share, jumping 42.00 pounds to close at 425.00 after trading in almost 14 million pounds.
Heliopolis gained 69.98 pounds to end the day at 500.00 but traded in only 935,000 pounds.

"It didn't start off being traded as freely as it ended up," Tahry said. "I think it's just testing the market. I think that there aren't shares available for trading. People might still believe the value is higher. They still might think there is room for more."
Commercial International Bank was the second most active share, closing 55.50 pounds higher at 600.00 after trade in more than 10 million pounds.
The bank made net profits of 180.887 million pounds ($53.2 million) in the first nine months of calendar 1996 compared to 168.505 million in the same period of 1995.
A tranche of the bank's shares have gone on sale internationally through a global depositary receipt.
Egyptian American Bank rose 5.00 pounds to 185.00 on its second day of official trade.
The CMAindex for openly traded firms rose to 502.32 from 479.5 points on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 212.93 from 205.31.
